headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Open Interpreter can alter local files and egress broadly while Prefect can consume workflow metadata, creating default-path leakage and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads the local filesystem and clipboard by default, and Prefect can ingest API/workflow inputs; a malicious file or copied content can steer Open Interpreter and then be propagated into Prefect workflows. The shared filesystem bridge makes this plausible, though not as direct as an MCP channel.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes artifacts produced by Open Interpreter from the shared filesystem or clipboard
IF a user pastes attacker-controlled content into Open Interpreter and then forwards its output into Prefect
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Use separate directories for each agent
Require manual review of any file before Prefect reads it
Run Open Interpreter in Docker mode
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and can call external APIs. If sensitive local files are processed by Open Interpreter and then surfaced into Prefect outputs or API calls, data can leak beyond the local machine. Prefect’s limited declared data classes reduce certainty, but the pathway exists.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter reads sensitive local files and emits them into a Prefect workflow artifact
IF Prefect sends workflow metadata derived from Open Interpreter output to an external API
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a narrow working directory
Redact secrets before passing outputs to Prefect
Block outbound network access for the pair during testing
Use separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; Prefect can also interact with APIs and orchestrate workflows. Because Open Interpreter shares state via filesystem and supports multiple instances, concurrent writes or git mutations can collide with Prefect-driven automation, risking irreversible repo or workflow corruption. The overlap is dangerous in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Prefect triggers actions while Open Interpreter is modifying git state or files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause Prefect runs while Open Interpreter edits the repo
Use file locks around shared mutable paths
Review git diffs before any commit
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code, edits, and shell actions that Prefect may treat as workflow inputs or metadata. If Prefect acts on those outputs without verification, a mistaken or malicious Open Interpreter result can cascade into automated downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Open Interpreter output as an authoritative workflow parameter
IF downstream Prefect tasks execute based on unreviewed Open Interpreter-generated facts
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before Prefect execution
Require schema validation on Open Interpreter outputs
Limit Prefect to read-only dry runs
Log and diff all generated parameters
requires-engineering: add signed output contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine, while Prefect is described as workflow-metadata oriented. No explicit residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is justified. The risk is mainly that local sensitive data could be moved into workflow metadata, but the profiles do not show a specific regulatory breach.
conditions: IF regulated data from the local machine is copied into Prefect workflow metadata
IF an operator routes personal data through Open Interpreter outputs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflow metadata
Mask identifiers before orchestration
Keep audit logs minimal
Confirm retention settings for any workflow store
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
